blocks.text: Day 4 · A visit to the Maleku Indigenous Reserve in northern Costa Rica, to learn how the community lives today and how it has rescued its traditions. Welcomed by the locals at Tonjibe Palenque, walk through the village to learn about their burial customs, the palenques built in ancient times, the crafts that support the community, the use of cacao in their agriculture and their traditional clothing, then follow a 600-metre forest path to discover the medicinal plants and trees used by their ancestors. Continue to the northern lowlands and La Fortuna, at the foot of Arenal Volcano, and relax in the area’s hot springs. Overnight at Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa. (B)

blocks.text: Arenal Volcano: Mistico and the 1968 trail

blocks.text:
Morning · The Arenal Hanging Bridges at Mistico Park, one of the best nature walks around La Fortuna: about 3 km of easy trails and 15 bridges, 6 of them hanging, bring you close to the birds, flowers and lush vegetation of the primary rainforest, with views of Arenal Volcano (about 2.5 hours).

Afternoon · A guided walk on the 1968 trail, along the edge of Arenal Volcano National Park, where parts of the landscape were devastated by the lava flows of 1968 and still have little vegetation: magnificent views of the volcano, Lake Arenal and the dormant volcano Cerro Chato, with forested sections where your guide will look for birds, monkeys and other wildlife. Overnight at Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa.
